sanskrit: arjunena vimuktas tu rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ cacāra pṛthivīṃ sarvām anirviṇṇas tathā kṛtaḥ
english: Released by Arjuna, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, roamed the whole earth thus humiliated, yet unbroken in spirit.

sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ vā manuṣyaṃ vā śṛṇute yaṃ balādhikam rāvaṇas taṃ samāsādya yuddhe hvayati darpitaḥ
english: Whoever Rāvaṇa heard of — rākṣasa or human — who excelled in strength, him he would approach in arrogance and challenge to battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit kiṣkindhāṃ nagarīṃ vālipālitām gatvāhvayati yuddhāya vālinaṃ hemamālinam
english: Then one day he went to Kiṣkindhā, the city governed by Vālin, and challenged to battle Vālin of the golden garland.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ vānarāmātyas tāras tārāpitā prabhuḥ uvāca rāvaṇaṃ vākyaṃ yuddhaprepsum upāgatam
english: Then Tāra, the monkey minister, father of Tārā, that lord, spoke these words to Rāvaṇa who had come eager for battle.

sanskrit: rākṣasendra gato vālī yas te pratibalo bhavet nānyaḥ pramukhataḥ sthātuṃ tava śaktaḥ plavaṃgamaḥ
english: "O lord of rākṣasas, Vālin has gone — he who would be your match in strength. No other monkey is capable of standing before you.

sanskrit: caturbhyo 'pi samudrebhyaḥ saṃdhyām anvāsya rāvaṇa imaṃ muhūrtam āyāti vālī tiṣṭha muhūrtakam
english: Rāvaṇa, he worships the twilight at all four oceans and will return in a moment. Wait but a moment.

sanskrit: etān asthicayān paśya ya ete śaṅkhapāṇḍurāḥ yuddhārthinām ime rājan vānarādhipatejasā
english: "See these heaps of bones, white as conch shells — these, O king, belong to those who came seeking battle and were consumed by the power of the monkey-lord.

sanskrit: yad vāmṛtarasaḥ pītas tvayā rāvaṇarākṣasa tathā vālinam āsādya tadantaṃ tava jīvitam
english: "Whatever nectar you have drunk, O Rāvaṇa the rākṣasa, once you encounter Vālin your life will end at that moment.

sanskrit: atha vā tvarase martuṃ gaccha dakṣiṇasāgaram vālinaṃ drakṣyase tatra bhūmiṣṭham iva bhāskaram
english: "Or if you are in haste to die, go to the southern ocean — you will see Vālin there, standing on the earth like the sun itself."

sanskrit: sa tu tāraṃ vinirbhartsya rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ puṣpakaṃ tat samāruhya prayayau dakṣiṇārṇavam
english: Rebuking Tāra, Rāvaṇa, that lord of rākṣasas, mounted Puṣpaka and flew to the southern ocean.

sanskrit: tatra hemagiriprakhyaṃ taruṇārkanibhānanam rāvaṇo vālinaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdhyopāsanatatparam
english: There Rāvaṇa saw Vālin, whose face glowed like the rising sun, resembling a mountain of gold, absorbed in twilight worship.

sanskrit: puṣpakād avaruhyātha rāvaṇo 'ñjanasaṃnibhaḥ grahītuṃ vālinaṃ tūrṇaṃ niḥśabdapadam ādravat
english: Rāvaṇa, dark as collyrium, descended from Puṣpaka and stealthily rushed forward to seize Vālin.

sanskrit: yadṛcchayonmīlayatā vālināpi sa rāvaṇaḥ pāpābhiprāyavān dṛṣṭaś cakāra na ca saṃbhramam
english: Vālin, who happened to open his eyes, also saw that Rāvaṇa, intent on evil, but did not grow alarmed.

sanskrit: śaśam ālakṣya siṃho vā pannagaṃ garuḍo yathā na cintayati taṃ vālī rāvaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam
english: As a lion does not concern itself with a rabbit, or Garuḍa with a serpent, so Vālin gave no thought to Rāvaṇa of evil resolve.

sanskrit: jighṛkṣamāṇam adyainaṃ rāvaṇaṃ pāpabuddhinam kakṣāvalambinaṃ kṛtvā gamiṣyāmi mahārṇavān
english: "I will take this Rāvaṇa of wicked mind who seeks to seize me, tuck him under my arm, and travel the great oceans.

sanskrit: drakṣyanty ariṃ mamāṅkasthaṃ sraṃsitorukarāmbaram lambamānaṃ daśagrīvaṃ garuḍasyeva pannagam
english: "They shall see my enemy seated in my lap, his garments slipping from his thighs, the ten-necked one dangling like a serpent in Garuḍa's grasp."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ matim āsthāya vālī karṇam upāśritaḥ japan vai naigamān mantrāṃs tasthau parvatarāḍ iva
english: Having thus resolved, Vālin, muttering Vedic mantras under his breath, remained still as the king of mountains.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ jighṛkṣantau harirākṣasapārthivau prayatnavantau tat karma īhatur baladarpitau
english: Both that monkey-king and the king of rākṣasas, each intent on seizing the other, proud of their strength, exerted themselves toward that deed.

sanskrit: hastagrāhyaṃ tu taṃ matvā pādaśabdena rāvaṇam parāṅmukho 'pi jagrāha vālī sarpam ivāṇḍajaḥ
english: Judging him close enough to grasp by hand, Vālin, even with his back turned, caught Rāvaṇa by the sound of his footstep, as a bird catches a serpent.

sanskrit: grahītukāmaṃ taṃ gṛhya rakṣasām īśvaraṃ hariḥ kham utpapāta vegena kṛtvā kakṣāvalambinam
english: Seizing that lord of rākṣasas who had come to seize him, the monkey leapt skyward with speed, having tucked him under his arm.

sanskrit: sa taṃ pīḍdayamānas tu vitudantaṃ nakhair muhuḥ jahāra rāvaṇaṃ vālī pavanas toyadaṃ yathā
english: Though Rāvaṇa was piercing him again and again with his nails, Vālin, oppressed by him, carried Rāvaṇa as the wind carries a rain-cloud.

sanskrit: atha te rākṣasāmātyā hriyamāṇe daśānane mumokṣayiṣavo ghorā ravamāṇā hy abhidravan
english: Then those terrible rākṣasa ministers, seeing the ten-headed one being carried away and wishing to free him, came rushing and roaring.

sanskrit: anvīyamānas tair vālī bhrājate 'mbaramadhyagaḥ anvīyamāno meghaughair ambarastha ivāṃśumān
english: Pursued by them, Vālin blazed in the midst of the sky — like the sun in the sky pursued by masses of clouds.

sanskrit: te 'śaknuvantaḥ saṃprāptaṃ vālinaṃ rākṣasottamāḥ tasya bāhūruvegena pariśrāntaḥ patanti ca
english: Those foremost rākṣasas, unable to overtake Vālin, exhausted by the force of his arms and legs, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: vālimārgād apākrāman parvatendrā hi gacchataḥ
english: The mountain lords drew back from Vālin's path as he flew past.

sanskrit: apakṣigaṇasaṃpāto vānarendro mahājavaḥ kramaśaḥ sāgarān sarvān saṃdhyākālam avandata
english: The monkey-lord, of immense speed, outstripping flocks of birds, paid homage to the twilight in succession at all the oceans.

sanskrit: sabhājyamāno bhūtais tu khecaraiḥ khecaro hariḥ paścimaṃ sāgaraṃ vālī ājagāma sarāvaṇaḥ
english: Honoured by sky-dwelling beings, the sky-ranging monkey Vālin reached the western ocean together with Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tatra saṃdhyām upāsitvā snātvā japtvā ca vānaraḥ uttaraṃ sāgaraṃ prāyād vahamāno daśānanam
english: There the monkey worshipped the twilight, bathed, and recited his prayers; then he proceeded to the northern ocean, still bearing the ten-headed one.

sanskrit: uttare sāgare saṃdhyām upāsitvā daśānanam vahamāno 'gamad vālī pūrvam ambumahānidhim
english: Having worshipped the twilight at the northern ocean, Vālin went, bearing the ten-headed one, to the great treasure of eastern waters.

sanskrit: tatrāpi saṃdhyām anvāsya vāsaviḥ sa harīśvaraḥ kiṣkindhābhimukho gṛhya rāvaṇaṃ punar āgamat
english: There too, having observed the twilight worship, that lord of monkeys, son of Vāsava, turned toward Kiṣkindhā, grasping Rāvaṇa, and came back.

sanskrit: caturṣv api samudreṣu saṃdhyām anvāsya vānaraḥ rāvaṇodvahanaśrāntaḥ kiṣkindhopavane 'patat
english: The monkey, having worshipped the twilight at all four oceans, weary from carrying Rāvaṇa, alighted in the forest of Kiṣkindhā.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ tu mumocātha svakakṣāt kapisattamaḥ kutas tvam iti covāca prahasan rāvaṇaṃ prati
english: Then that best of monkeys released Rāvaṇa from his arm and, laughing, asked Rāvaṇa: "Where do you come from?"

sanskrit: vismayaṃ tu mahad gatvā śramalokanirīkṣaṇaḥ rākṣaseśo harīśaṃ tam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seized by great amazement, looking about with exhausted eyes, the lord of rākṣasas spoke these words to that lord of monkeys:

sanskrit: vānarendra mahendrābha rākṣasendro 'smi rāvaṇaḥ yuddhepsur ahaṃ saṃprāptaḥ sa cādyāsāditas tvayā
english: "O lord of monkeys, radiant as great Indra, I am Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas. I came here eager for battle, and today I have indeed encountered you.

sanskrit: aho balam aho vīryam aho gambhīratā ca te yenāhaṃ paśuvad gṛhya bhrāmitaś caturo 'rṇavān
english: "Ah, what strength! Ah, what heroism! Ah, what composure you possess — by which, seizing me like an animal, you have carried me around the four oceans!

sanskrit: evam aśrāntavad vīra śīghram eva ca vānara māṃ caivodvahamānas tu ko 'nyo vīraḥ kramiṣyati
english: "O hero, O monkey, bearing me thus as if untiring and with such speed — what other hero could traverse thus?

sanskrit: trayāṇām eva bhūtānāṃ gatir eṣā plavaṃgama mano'nilasuparṇānāṃ tava vā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "This speed belongs to only three beings, O leaping one: the mind, the wind, and Suparṇa — or you; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ dṛṣṭabalas tubhyam icchāmi haripuṃgava tvayā saha ciraṃ sakhyaṃ susnigdhaṃ pāvakāgrataḥ
english: "I, who have now seen your strength, O foremost of monkeys, desire a lasting and deeply affectionate friendship with you, before the sacred fire.

sanskrit: dārāḥ putrāḥ puraṃ rāṣṭraṃ bhogācchādanabhojanam sarvam evāvibhaktaṃ nau bhaviṣyati harīśvara
english: "Wives, sons, city, kingdom, pleasures, garments, food — all of this shall be undivided between us two, O lord of monkeys."

sanskrit: tataḥ prajvālayitvāgniṃ tāv ubhau harirākṣasau bhrātṛtvam upasaṃpannau pariṣvajya parasparam
english: Then the two — monkey and rākṣasa — kindled a fire, attained brotherhood, and embraced one another.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ lambitakarau tatas tau harirākṣasau kiṣkindhāṃ viśatur hṛṣṭau siṃhau giriguhām iva
english: Clasping each other's hands, those two — monkey and rākṣasa — joyfully entered Kiṣkindhā, like two lions entering a mountain cave.

sanskrit: sa tatra māsam uṣitaḥ sugrīva iva rāvaṇaḥ amātyair āgatair nīcas trailokyotsādanārthbhiḥ
english: Rāvaṇa dwelt there for a month, like Sugrīva, when his ministers arrived to fetch him — that low one who sought to destroy the three worlds.

sanskrit: evam etat purāvṛttaṃ vālinā rāvaṇaḥ prabho dharṣitaś ca kṛtaś cāpi bhrātā pāvakasaṃnidhau
english: "Thus was this event of the past, O lord: Rāvaṇa was humbled by Vālin and then also made a brother in the presence of fire.

sanskrit: balam apratimaṃ rāma vālino 'bhavad uttamam so 'pi tayā vinirdagdhaḥ śalabho vahninā yathā
english: "The strength of Vālin, O Rāma, was matchless and supreme; yet even he was consumed by that fate, like a moth by fire."

sanskrit: apṛcchata tato rāmo dakṣiṇāśālayaṃ munim prāñjalir vinayopeta idam āha vaco 'rthavat
english: Then Rāma questioned the sage who dwelt in the southern hall; standing with joined palms, endowed with humility, he spoke this meaningful speech:

sanskrit: atulaṃ balam etābhyāṃ vālino rāvaṇasya ca na tv etau hanumadvīryaiḥ samāv iti matir mama
english: "The strength of these two — Vālin and Rāvaṇa — was incomparable; yet my view is that neither of them was equal to Hanumān in valour.

sanskrit: śauryaṃ dākṣyaṃ balaṃ dhairyaṃ prājñatā nayasādhanam vikramaś ca prabhāvaś ca hanūmati kṛtālayāḥ
english: "Courage, dexterity, strength, steadiness, wisdom, mastery of policy, heroism, and power — all these have their home in Hanumān.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvodadhiṃ viṣīdantīṃ tadaiṣa kapivāhinīm samāśvāsya kapīn bhūyo yojanānāṃ śataṃ plutaḥ
english: "When the army of monkeys was despondent at the sight of the ocean, he alone reassured the monkeys and then leapt a hundred yojanas.

sanskrit: dharṣayitvā purīṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā saṃbhāṣitā cāpi sītā viśvāsitā tathā
english: "He assaulted the city of Laṅkā and the inner apartments of Rāvaṇa; he found Sītā, spoke with her, and reassured her.

sanskrit: senāgragā mantrisutāḥ kiṃkarā rāvaṇātmajaḥ ete hanumatā tatra ekena vinipātitāḥ
english: "The vanguard of the army, the sons of ministers, the servants, the sons of Rāvaṇa — all these were felled there by Hanumān alone.

sanskrit: bhūyo bandhād vimuktena saṃbhāṣitvā daśānanam laṅkā bhasmīkṛtā tena pāvakeneva medinī
english: "Released again from captivity, having spoken with the ten-headed one, he reduced Laṅkā to ashes as fire reduces the earth.

sanskrit: na kālasya na śakrasya na viṣṇor vittapasya ca karmāṇi tāni śrūyante yāni yuddhe hanūmataḥ
english: "Neither of Kāla, nor of Śakra, nor of Viṣṇu, nor of Kubera are such deeds as Hanumān's in battle heard of.

sanskrit: etasya bāhuvīryeṇa laṅkā sītā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ prāpto mayā jayaś caiva rājyaṃ mitrāṇi bāndhavāḥ
english: "By the arm-strength of this one, I obtained Laṅkā, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, victory, the kingdom, friends, and kinsmen.

sanskrit: hanūmān yadi me na syād vānarādhipateḥ sakhā pravṛttam api ko vettuṃ jānakyāḥ śaktimān bhavet
english: "If Hanumān, friend of the monkey-lord, were not with me, who would have been capable of obtaining even news of Jānakī?

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ vālī caitena sugrīvapriyakāmyayā tadā vaire samutpanne na dagdho vīrudho yathā
english: "Why did Hanumān, desiring the welfare of Sugrīva, not burn Vālin like a creeper when that enmity arose?

sanskrit: na hi veditavān manye hanūmān ātmano balam yad dṛṣṭavāñ jīviteṣṭaṃ kliśyantaṃ vānarādhipam
english: "I believe Hanumān did not know his own strength, since he merely witnessed the monkey-lord, dear to him, being tormented.

sanskrit: etan me bhagavan sarvaṃ hanūmati mahāmune vistareṇa yathātattvaṃ kathayāmarapūjita
english: "All of this concerning Hanumān, O Blessed One, O great sage, O you worshipped by the immortals — tell me in full detail and in truth."

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetuyuktam ṛṣis tataḥ hanūmataḥ samakṣaṃ tam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having heard Rāghava's reasoned speech, the sage then spoke these words in the presence of Hanumān himself:

sanskrit: satyam etad raghuśreṣṭha yad bravīṣi hanūmataḥ na bale vidyate tulyo na gatau na matau paraḥ
english: "This is true, O foremost of the Raghu line, what you say of Hanumān. In strength there is none equal to him, nor in speed, nor in intelligence.

sanskrit: amoghaśāpaiḥ śāpas tu datto 'sya ṛṣibhiḥ purā na veditā balaṃ yena balī sann arimardanaḥ
english: "But a curse was placed upon him in the past by sages whose curses never fail — that he, though mighty, the crusher of enemies, would not know his own strength.

sanskrit: bālye 'py etena yat karma kṛtaṃ rāma mahābala tan na varṇayituṃ śakyam atibālatayāsya te
english: "Even the deeds performed by him in childhood, O Rāma of great strength, cannot be adequately described on account of his extreme youth at the time.

sanskrit: yadi vāsti tv abhiprāyas tac chrotuṃ tava rāghava samādhāya matiṃ rāma niśāmaya vadāmy aham
english: "But if, O Rāghava, you have desire to hear it, collect your mind, O Rāma, and listen — I shall tell it.

sanskrit: sūryadattavarasvarṇaḥ sumerur nāma parvataḥ yatra rājyaṃ praśāsty asya keṣarī nāma vai pitā
english: "There is a mountain named Sumeru, of gold granted as a boon by the Sun; there his father — Keśarī by name — governs a kingdom.

sanskrit: tasya bhāryā babhūveṣṭā hy añjaneti pariśrutā janayām āsa tasyāṃ vai vāyur ātmajam uttamam
english: "His beloved wife was known as Añjanā. In her, Vāyu begot a most excellent son.

sanskrit: śāliśūkasamābhāsaṃ prāsūtemaṃ tadāñjanā phalāny āhartukāmā vai niṣkrāntā gahane carā
english: "Having given birth to this one, bright as a śāli-grain husk, Añjanā had gone out roaming the forest, desiring to gather fruits.

sanskrit: eṣa mātur viyogāc ca kṣudhayā ca bhṛśārditaḥ ruroda śiśur atyarthaṃ śiśuḥ śarabharāḍ iva
english: "This infant, greatly afflicted by the absence of its mother and by hunger, wept intensely, like the young of the king of śarabhas.

sanskrit: tatodyantaṃ vivasvantaṃ japāpuṣpotkaropamam dadṛśe phalalobhāc ca utpapāta raviṃ prati
english: "Then, seeing the rising Vivasvat, resembling a cluster of hibiscus flowers, and tempted by it as a fruit, he leapt upward toward the sun.

sanskrit: bālārkābhimukho bālo bālārka iva mūrtimān grahītukāmo bālārkaṃ plavate 'mbaramadhyagaḥ
english: "The child, facing the morning sun, himself like the morning sun made manifest, desiring to seize the morning sun, flew through the middle of the sky.

sanskrit: etasmin plavamāne tu śiśubhāve hanūmati devadānavasiddhānāṃ vismayaḥ sumahān abhūt
english: "While Hanumān was thus flying in his infant state, a very great astonishment arose among the gods, dānavas, and siddhas.

sanskrit: nāpy evaṃ vegavān vāyur garuḍo na manas tathā yathāyaṃ vāyuputras tu kramate 'mbaram uttamam
english: "Neither the wind is so swift, nor Garuḍa, nor the mind — as this son of Vāyu traverses the high sky.

sanskrit: yadi tāvac chiśor asya īdṛśau gativikramau yauvanaṃ balam āsādya kathaṃ vego bhaviṣyati
english: "If even as an infant his speed and stride are like this, what will his swiftness be when he attains the strength of youth?

sanskrit: tam anuplavate vāyuḥ plavantaṃ putram ātmanaḥ sūryadāhabhayād rakṣaṃs tuṣāracayaśītalaḥ
english: "Vāyu flew after his own son as he flew, protecting him out of fear of the sun's burning rays, cooling him with masses of frost-cold air.

sanskrit: bahuyojanasāhasraṃ kramaty eṣa tato 'mbaram pitur balāc ca bālyāc ca bhāskarābhyāśam āgataḥ
english: "Traversing many thousands of yojanas through the sky, he reached the proximity of the sun, by the strength of his father and by the recklessness of childhood.

sanskrit: śiśur eṣa tv adoṣajña iti matvā divākaraḥ kāryaṃ cātra samāyattam ity evaṃ na dadāha saḥ
english: "The day-maker, thinking 'this is a child, unknowing of fault,' and knowing too that a purpose was bound up in this, did not burn him.

sanskrit: yam eva divasaṃ hy eṣa grahītuṃ bhāskaraṃ plutaḥ tam eva divasaṃ rāhur jighṛkṣati divākaram
english: "On the very same day that he leapt to seize the sun, Rāhu also was seeking to swallow the day-maker.

sanskrit: anena ca parāmṛṣṭo rāma sūryarathopari apakrāntas tatas trasto rāhuś candrārkamardanaḥ
english: "Rāhu, the devourer of moon and sun, touched by this child on top of the sun's chariot, fled in fear.

sanskrit: sa indrabhavanaṃ gatvā saroṣaḥ siṃhikāsutaḥ abravīd bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā devaṃ devagaṇair vṛtam
english: "The son of Siṃhikā, incensed, went to Indra's palace and, furrowing his brow, spoke to the god surrounded by the host of gods:

sanskrit: bubhukṣāpanayaṃ dattvā candrārkau mama vāsava kim idaṃ tat tvayā dattam anyasya balavṛtrahan
english: "'You gave me moon and sun for appeasing my hunger, O Vāsava — what is this you have now given them to another, O mighty slayer of Vṛtra?

sanskrit: adyāhaṃ parvakāle tu jighṛkṣuḥ sūryam āgataḥ athānyo rāhur āsādya jagrāha sahasā ravim
english: "'Today I came at the conjunction time, wishing to seize the sun; but some other Rāhu, having arrived there, suddenly seized the sun!'"

sanskrit: sa rāhor vacanaṃ śrutvā vāsavaḥ saṃbhramānvitaḥ utpapātāsanaṃ hitvā udvahan kāñcanasrajam
english: "Hearing Rāhu's words, Vāsava was seized with agitation; he leapt up from his seat, lifting his golden garland.

sanskrit: tataḥ kailāsakūṭābhaṃ caturdantaṃ madasravam śṛṅgārakāriṇaṃ prāṃśuṃ svarṇaghaṇṭāṭṭahāsinam
english: "Then the great Airāvata, white as the peak of Kailāsa, with four tusks, streaming with rut-fluid, causing delight, tall, laughing loudly with its golden bell —

sanskrit: indraḥ karīndram āruhya rāhuṃ kṛtvā puraḥsaram prāyād yatrābhavat sūryaḥ sahānena hanūmatā
english: "— Indra mounted that king of elephants and, placing Rāhu in front, went to where the sun was, together with Hanumān.

sanskrit: athātirabhasenāgād rāhur utsṛjya vāsavam anena ca sa vai dṛṣṭa ādhāvañ śailakūṭavat
english: "Then Rāhu, having rushed forward in great haste and left Vāsava behind, was seen by Hanumān, who rushed at him like a mountain peak.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūryaṃ samutsṛjya rāhum evam avekṣya ca utpapāta punar vyoma grahītuṃ siṃhikāsutam
english: "Then, releasing the sun and seeing Rāhu thus, Hanumān leapt again into the sky to seize the son of Siṃhikā.

sanskrit: utsṛjyārkam imaṃ rāma ādhāvantaṃ plavaṃgamam dṛṣṭvā rāhuḥ parāvṛtya mukhaśeṣaḥ parāṅmukhaḥ
english: "O Rāma, seeing the leaping one rush toward him having released the sun, Rāhu, that one who is nothing but a mouth, turned his face and fled.

sanskrit: indram āśaṃsamānas tu trātāraṃ siṃhikāsutaḥ indra indreti saṃtrāsān muhur muhur abhāṣata
english: "Hoping for Indra as protector, the son of Siṃhikā cried out again and again in terror: 'Indra! Indra!'

sanskrit: rāhor vikrośamānasya prāg evālakṣitaḥ svaraḥ śrutvendrovāca mā bhaiṣīr ayam enaṃ nihanmy aham
english: "Indra had already noticed the voice of the screaming Rāhu; having heard it, Indra said: 'Do not fear — I shall kill this one.'

sanskrit: airāvataṃ tato dṛṣṭvā mahat tad idam ity api phalaṃ taṃ hastirājānam abhidudrāva mārutiḥ
english: "Then, seeing the great Airāvata, thinking 'this too is a fruit,' the son of the wind rushed toward that king of elephants.

sanskrit: tadāsya dhāvato rūpam airāvatajighṛkṣayā muhūrtam abhavad ghoram indrāgnyor iva bhāsvaram
english: "Then, as he rushed to seize Airāvata, his form for a moment became terrible, blazing like Indra and Agni combined.

sanskrit: evam ādhāvamānaṃ tu nātikruddhaḥ śacīpatiḥ hastāntenātimuktena kuliśenābhyatāḍayat
english: "The husband of Śacī, not excessively angered, struck with the thunderbolt released from the tip of his hand the one who was rushing thus.

sanskrit: tato girau papātaiṣa indravajrābhitāḍitaḥ patamānasya caitasya vāmo hanur abhajyata
english: "Then, struck by Indra's thunderbolt, Hanumān fell upon a mountain; as he fell, his left jaw was broken.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu patite bāle vajratāḍanavihvale cukrodhendrāya pavanaḥ prajānām aśivāya ca
english: "When the child fell, reeling from the blow of the thunderbolt — to the misfortune of all creatures — Pavana grew furious at Indra.

sanskrit: viṇmūtrāśayam āvṛtya prajāsv antargataḥ prabhuḥ rurodha sarvabhūtāni yathā varṣāṇi vāsavaḥ
english: "That lord entered all living beings, stopping up the cavities of waste and urine, and withheld all creatures, as Vāsava withholds the rains.

sanskrit: vāyuprakopād bhūtāni nirucchvāsāni sarvataḥ saṃdhibhir bhajyamānāni kāṣṭhabhūtāni jajñire
english: "By reason of Vāyu's wrath, all beings everywhere, bereft of breath, with their joints cracking, became like blocks of wood.

sanskrit: niḥsvadhaṃ nirvaṣaṭkāraṃ niṣkriyaṃ dharmavarjitam vāyuprakopāt trailokyaṃ nirayastham ivābabhau
english: "By Vāyu's wrath, the three worlds, devoid of svadha-offerings, devoid of vaṣaṭ-calls, devoid of activity, bereft of dharma, appeared like those fallen to hell.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajāḥ sagandharvāḥ sadevāsuramānuṣāḥ prajāpatiṃ samādhāvann asukhārtāḥ sukhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: "Then all creatures — together with gandharvas, gods, asuras, and humans — rushed to Prajāpati, suffering in their misery, seeking happiness.

sanskrit: ūcuḥ prāñjalayo devā darodaranibhodarāḥ tvayā sma bhagavan sṛṣṭāḥ prajānātha caturvidhāḥ
english: "The gods, with joined palms and bellies shrunken with fear, said: 'By you, O Blessed Lord, we four kinds of creatures have been created, O lord of creatures.

sanskrit: tvayā datto 'yam asmākam āyuṣaḥ pavanaḥ patiḥ so 'smān prāṇeśvaro bhūtvā kasmād eṣo 'dya sattama
english: "'By you, Vāyu was given to us as the lord of life-breath. Having become our lord of prāṇa, why is he today, O best of beings —

sanskrit: rurodha duḥkhaṃ janayann antaḥpura iva striyaḥ tasmāt tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptā vāyunopahatā vibho
english: "'— blocking and causing suffering, like women shut within the inner apartments? Therefore, afflicted by Vāyu, we have come to you for refuge, O mighty one.

sanskrit: vāyusaṃrodhajaṃ duḥkham idaṃ no nuda śatruhan
english: "'Remove this suffering of ours born from the obstruction of Vāyu, O slayer of enemies!'

sanskrit: etat prajānāṃ śrutvā tu prajānāthaḥ prajāpatiḥ kāraṇād iti tān uktvā prajāḥ punar abhāṣata
english: "Hearing this from the creatures, Prajāpati, the lord of creatures, saying 'I know the reason,' spoke again to them:

sanskrit: yasmin vaḥ kāraṇe vāyuś cukrodha ca rurodha ca prajāḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ tat sarvaṃ śrotavyaṃ cātmanaḥ kṣamam
english: "'The reason for which Vāyu grew wrathful and obstructed — hear all of that, O creatures, and what is fitting for you yourselves to bear.

sanskrit: putras tasyāmareśena indreṇādya nipātitaḥ rāhor vacanam ājñāya rājñā vaḥ kopito 'nilaḥ
english: "'His son has been struck down today by Indra, king of the immortals, who acted on Rāhu's word — this is why Anila is angry with you all.'

sanskrit: aśarīraḥ śarīreṣu vāyuś carati pālayan śarīraṃ hi vinā vāyuṃ samatāṃ yāti reṇubhiḥ
english: "'Vāyu, bodiless himself, moves through bodies sustaining them; for a body without Vāyu becomes equal to dust.

sanskrit: vāyuḥ prāṇāḥ sukhaṃ vāyur vāyuḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat vāyunā saṃparityaktaṃ na sukhaṃ vindate jagat
english: "'Vāyu is the life-breath, Vāyu is happiness, Vāyu is all this world; a world abandoned by Vāyu finds no happiness.'

sanskrit: adyaiva ca parityaktaṃ vāyunā jagad āyuṣā adyaiveme nirucchvāsāḥ kāṣṭhakuḍyopamāḥ sthitāḥ
english: "'Today the world has been abandoned by Vāyu, who is life itself; today these beings stand breathless, like wood and walls.'

sanskrit: tad yāmas tatra yatrāste māruto rukprado hi vaḥ mā vināśaṃ gamiṣyāma aprasādyāditeḥ sutam
english: "'Therefore let us go to where Māruta dwells — for he is the source of your affliction. Lest we perish, let us not fail to propitiate the son of Aditi's co-wife.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prajābhiḥ sahitaḥ prajāpatiḥ sadevagandharvabhujaṃgaguhyakaḥ jagāma tatrāsyati yatra mārutaḥ sutaṃ surendrābhihataṃ pragṛhya saḥ
english: "Then Prajāpati, together with the creatures and with gods, gandharvas, serpents, and guhyakas, went to where Māruta sat, holding his son who had been struck down by the lord of the immortals.

sanskrit: tato 'rkavaiśvānarakāñcanaprabhaṃ sutaṃ tadotsaṅgagataṃ sadāgateḥ caturmukho vīkṣya kṛpām athākarot sadevasiddharṣibhujaṃgarākṣasaḥ
english: "Then the four-faced one, seeing the son of ever-moving Vāyu in his lap, glowing like sun and fire and gold, was moved to compassion, together with the gods, siddhas, sages, serpents, and rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmahaṃ dṛṣṭvā vāyuḥ putravadhārditaḥ śiśukaṃ taṃ samādāya uttasthau dhātur agrataḥ
english: Then Vāyu, afflicted by the wounding of his son, took up the infant and rose to stand before the Fashioner, the Grandfather.

sanskrit: calatkuṇḍalamaulisraktapanīyavibhūṣaṇaḥ pādayor nyapatad vāyus tisro 'vasthāya vedhase
english: With earrings, crown, and red-water ornaments trembling, Vāyu fell at the feet of the Creator, composing himself in the three-fold posture of reverence.

sanskrit: taṃ tu vedavidādyas tu lambābharaṇaśobhinā vāyum utthāpya hastena śiśuṃ taṃ parimṛṣṭavān
english: That foremost knower of the Vedas, radiant with pendant ornaments, raising Vāyu up by the hand, touched the infant gently.

sanskrit: spṛṣṭamātras tataḥ so 'tha salīlaṃ padmajanmanā jalasiktaṃ yathā sasyaṃ punar jīvitam āptavān
english: Merely touched by him who was born from the lotus, the child gracefully regained life, like a crop revived by water.

sanskrit: prāṇavantam imaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāṇo gandhavaho mudā cacāra sarvabhūteṣu saṃniruddhaṃ yathāpurā
english: Seeing this one restored to life, Prāṇa, the sweet-bearing wind, joyfully moved through all beings as before, unobstructed.

sanskrit: marudrogavinirmuktāḥ prajā vai muditābhavan śītavātavinirmuktāḥ padminya iva sāmbujāḥ
english: Freed from the disease of the wind's restraint, all creatures became joyful, like lotus-ponds freed from cold winds, bearing their flowers again.

sanskrit: tatas triyugmas trikakut tridhāmā tridaśārcitaḥ uvāca devatā brahmā mārutapriyakāmyayā
english: Then Brahmā, the triple-aged, three-peaked, three-aboded, worshipped by the thirty gods, spoke to the gods, desiring to please Māruta:

sanskrit: bho mahendrāgnivaruṇadhaneśvaramaheśvarāḥ jānatām api tat sarvaṃ hitaṃ vakṣyāmi śrūyatām
english: "O Mahendra, Agni, Varuṇa, Lord of wealth, and Maheśvara — I shall speak what is beneficial; though you know it, let it be heard.

sanskrit: anena śiśunā kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ vo bhaviṣyati dadatāsya varān sarve mārutasyāsya tuṣṭidān
english: "There is a great task for you all to be accomplished by this child. Let all of you give boons to him, the boons that please this Māruta."

sanskrit: tataḥ sahasranayanaḥ prītiraktaḥ śubhānanaḥ kuśe śayamayīṃ mālāṃ samutkṣipyedam abravīt
english: Then the thousand-eyed one, his face flushed with joy and beautiful, raising the kuśa-grass garland on which he lay, spoke thus:

sanskrit: matkarotsṛṣṭavajreṇa hanur asya yathā kṣataḥ nāmnaiṣa kapiśārdūlo bhavitā hanumān iti
english: "As his jaw (hanu) was injured by the thunderbolt released from my hand, by that name this tiger among monkeys shall be known as Hanumān.

sanskrit: aham evāsya dāsyāmi paramaṃ varam uttamam ataḥ prabhṛti vajrasya mamāvadhyo bhaviṣyati
english: "I myself shall give him the highest and best boon: from this day forward he shall be invulnerable to my thunderbolt."

sanskrit: mārtāṇḍas tv abravīt tatra bhagavāṃs timirāpahaḥ tejaso 'sya madīyasya dadāmi śatikāṃ kalām
english: "Then the Blessed Lord Mārtāṇḍa, dispeller of darkness, spoke there: 'I give him one-hundredth part of my own radiance.

sanskrit: yadā tu śāstrāṇy adhyetuṃ śaktir asya bhaviṣyati tadāsya śāstraṃ dāsyāmi yena vāgmī bhaviṣyati
english: "'When he shall have the capacity to study the sciences, I shall give him the knowledge of śāstras by which he will become eloquent.'"

sanskrit: varuṇaś ca varaṃ prādān nāsya mṛtyur bhaviṣyati varṣāyutaśatenāpi matpāśād udakād api
english: Varuṇa also granted a boon: "He shall not die — not for ten million years, and not from my noose, not from water."

sanskrit: yamo 'pi daṇḍāvadhyatvam arogatvaṃ ca nityaśaḥ diśate 'sya varaṃ tuṣṭa aviṣādaṃ ca saṃyuge
english: Yama too, pleased, granted his boon — immunity from the staff of death, perpetual freedom from disease, and cheerfulness in battle.

sanskrit: gadeyaṃ māmikā nainaṃ saṃyugeṣu vadhiṣyati ity evaṃ varadaḥ prāha tadā hy ekākṣipiṅgalaḥ
english: "My own mace shall not slay him in battles" — thus spoke the boon-granting one, he of the single tawny eye, Kubera.

sanskrit: matto madāyudhānāṃ ca na vadhyo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati ity evaṃ śaṃkareṇāpi datto 'sya paramo varaḥ
english: "He shall not be slain by me nor by the weapons of those intoxicated with power" — thus the supreme boon was also given by Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ brahmadaṇḍānām avadhyo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati dīrghāyuś ca mahātmā ca iti brahmābravīd vacaḥ
english: "He shall be invulnerable to all of Brahmā's weapons, long-lived and great-souled" — thus spoke Brahmā.

sanskrit: viśvakarmā tu dṛṣṭvainaṃ bālasūryopamaṃ śiśum śilpināṃ pravaraḥ prāha varam asya mahāmatiḥ
english: Viśvakarmā, seeing this infant resembling the infant sun, the foremost of craftsmen, of great wisdom, proclaimed his boon:

sanskrit: vinirmitāni devānām āyudhānīha yāni tu teṣāṃ saṃgrāmakāle tu avadhyo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Among all the weapons fashioned by me for the gods, he shall be invulnerable to any of them in the time of battle."

sanskrit: tataḥ surāṇāṃ tu varair dṛṣṭvā hy enam alaṃkṛtam caturmukhas tuṣṭamukho vāyum āha jagadguruḥ
english: Then, seeing him adorned with the boons of the gods, the four-faced one, the teacher of the world, with a pleased countenance, spoke to Vāyu:

sanskrit: amitrāṇāṃ bhayakaro mitrāṇām abhayaṃkaraḥ ajeyo bhavitā te 'tra putro mārutamārutiḥ
english: "Your son, son of Māruta, shall be the cause of fear to enemies and the giver of fearlessness to friends — unconquerable here.

sanskrit: rāvaṇotsādanārthāni rāmaprītikarāṇi ca romaharṣakarāṇy eṣa kartā karmāṇi saṃyuge
english: "He shall accomplish in battle deeds that shall overthrow Rāvaṇa, that shall bring joy to Rāma, and that shall make the hair stand on end."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tam āmantrya mārutaṃ te 'maraiḥ saha yathāgataṃ yayuḥ sarve pitāmahapurogamāḥ
english: Having spoken thus and bidding farewell to Māruta, all of them — with the Grandfather at the head — departed with the immortals as they had come.

sanskrit: so 'pi gandhavahaḥ putraṃ pragṛhya gṛham ānayat añjanāyāstam ākhyāya varaṃ dattaṃ viniḥsṛtaḥ
english: And Vāyu, the sweet-bearing wind, took his son, brought him home, told Añjanā of the boon that had been granted, and departed.

sanskrit: prāpya rāma varān eṣa varadānabalānvitaḥ balenātmani saṃsthena so 'pūryata yathārṇavaḥ
english: Having received these boons, O Rāma, he was filled with the power of the granted boons, with strength abiding in himself, as an ocean is filled.

sanskrit: balenāpūryamāṇo hi eṣa vānarapuṃgavaḥ āśrameṣu maharṣīṇām aparādhyati nirbhayaḥ
english: This foremost of monkeys, being filled with strength, fearlessly committed offenses in the hermitages of the great sages.

sanskrit: srugbhāṇḍān agnihotraṃ ca valkalānāṃ ca saṃcayān bhagnavicchinnavidhvastān suśāntānāṃ karoty ayam
english: He would break the ladles and vessels, destroy the agnihotra fires, and scatter the piles of bark garments of the tranquil sages, leaving them broken, torn, and ruined.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ brahmadaṇḍānām avadhyaṃ brahmaṇā kṛtam jānanta ṛṣayas taṃ vai kṣamante tasya nityaśaḥ
english: The sages, knowing that Brahmā had made him invulnerable to all of Brahmā's weapons, always bore with him.

sanskrit: yadā keṣariṇā tv eṣa vāyunā sāñjanena ca pratiṣiddho 'pi maryādāṃ laṅghayaty eva vānaraḥ
english: When even though restrained by Keśarī and by Vāyu and by Añjanā, this monkey continues to transgress all bounds —

sanskrit: tato maharṣayaḥ kruddhā bhṛgvaṅgirasavaṃśajāḥ śepur enaṃ raghuśreṣṭha nātikruddhātimanyavaḥ
english: — then the great sages, of the lineage of Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, O foremost of the Raghu line, cursed him — not with excessive anger or extreme wrath:

sanskrit: bādhase yat samāśritya balam asmān plavaṃgama tad dīrghakālaṃ vettāsi nāsmākaṃ śāpamohitaḥ
english: "'O leaping one, you harass us relying on that strength — bewildered by our curse, you shall not know it for a long time.'

sanskrit: tatas tu hṛtatejaujā maharṣivacanaujasā eṣo śramāṇi nātyeti mṛdubhāvagataś caran
english: Then, with his radiance and power taken away by the power of the great sages' words, he roamed without exceeding his bounds, having attained a gentle nature.

sanskrit: atha ṛkṣarajā nāma vālisugrīvayoḥ pitā sarvavānararājāsīt tejasā iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Now there was one named Ṛkṣarājā, father of Vālin and Sugrīva, king of all the monkeys, blazing in splendour like the sun.

sanskrit: sa tu rājyaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā vānarāṇāṃ harīśvaraḥ tatas tvarkṣarajā nāma kāladharmeṇa saṃgataḥ
english: That lord of monkeys, having long governed the kingdom of the monkeys, passed away in the course of time — that one named Ṛkṣarājā met his death by the law of Time.

sanskrit: tasminn astamite vālī mantribhir mantrakovidaiḥ pitrye pade kṛto rājā sugrīvo vālinaḥ pade
english: When he had set, Vālin was made king in his father's place by ministers skilled in counsel, and Sugrīva in Vālin's place.

sanskrit: sugrīveṇa samaṃ tv asya advaidhaṃ chidravarjitam ahāryaṃ sakhyam abhavad anilasya yathāgninā
english: With Sugrīva, his friendship was undivided, without flaw, unshakeable — like that of Anila with fire.

sanskrit: eṣa śāpavaśād eva na vedabalam ātmanaḥ vālisugrīvayor vairaṃ yadā rāma samutthitam
english: It is only by the power of the curse that he did not know his own strength — when the enmity between Vālin and Sugrīva arose, O Rāma.

sanskrit: na hy eṣa rāma sugrīvo bhrāmyamāṇo 'pi vālinā vedayāno na ca hy eṣa balam ātmani mārutiḥ
english: "For, O Rāma, Sugrīva, even while being tormented by Vālin, did not know it, and Māruti did not know the strength within himself.

sanskrit: parākramotsāhamatipratāpaiḥ sauśīlyamādhuryanayānayaiś ca gāmbhīryacāturyasuvīryadhairyair hanūmataḥ ko 'py adhiko 'sti loke
english: "In valour, energy, intellect, and splendour, in virtue, sweetness, policy and its opposite, in gravity, cleverness, heroism, and steadfastness — who in this world surpasses Hanumān?

sanskrit: asau purā vyākaraṇaṃ grahīṣyan sūryonmukhaḥ pṛṣṭhagamaḥ kapīndraḥ udyadgirer astagiriṃ jagāma granthaṃ mahad dhārayad aprameyaḥ
english: "Long ago, to learn grammar, this immeasurable king of monkeys, facing the sun, moving backward, went from the rising mountain to the setting mountain, bearing that great text.

sanskrit: pravīvikṣor iva sāgarasya lokān didhakṣor iva pāvakasya lokakṣayeṣv eva yathāntakasya hanūmataḥ sthāsyati kaḥ purastāt
english: "Who shall stand before Hanumān — like the ocean that seeks to flood the worlds, like fire that seeks to burn them, like Antaka at the time of the world's destruction?

sanskrit: eṣo 'pi cānye ca mahākapīndrāḥ sugrīvamaindadvividāḥ sanīlāḥ satāratāreyanalāḥ sarambhās tvatkāraṇād rāma surair hi sṛṣṭāḥ
english: "He and the other great monkey-lords — Sugrīva, Mainda, Dvivida, together with Nīla, together with Tāra, Tāreya, Nala — all of these, O Rāma, were created by the gods for your sake.

sanskrit: tad etat kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi hanūmato bālabhāve karmaitat kathitaṃ mayā
english: "All of this has been told — what you asked of me. The deeds of Hanumān in his childhood have been narrated by me.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaḥ saṃbhāṣitaś cāsi rāma gacchamahe vayam evam uktvā gatāḥ sarve ṛṣayas te yathāgatam
english: "You have been seen, O Rāma, and spoken with. We shall go." Having spoken thus, all those sages departed as they had come.
